2010_012_101910regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, October 19, 2010, 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. It carries the minutes of the October 5, 2010 meeting and October 12, 2010 workshop, the September 2010 Treasurer's Report with a complete Pentamation check register plus ACH and wire-transfer schedules, a copy paper bid award to Midland Paper at $64,950.48, one teacher hire, an APT to Succeed curriculum report, the 2009/2010 Plante & Moran audit, and proposed Troy Youth Assistance by-law revisions. Total disbursements in the period are reported as $5,871,091.37.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting, Tuesday, October 19, 2010, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognitions**
Martell Elementary fifth graders who won the 2009/2010 Red Ribbon Song Writing Contest sponsored by Troy Families for Safe Homes and The Troy Coalition, for the song "Don't Let Drugs Get in the Way of Your Dreams" written with teacher Andrea Moon in October, 2009; a district-wide Fourth Grade Hit Song Contest was announced by Bemis vocal music teacher Emily Jambeau. A resolution honors forty-two 2010/2011 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, drawn from more than one million entrants at some 22,000 high schools, of whom 16,000 were named semifinalists, requiring PSAT scores in the top one and one-half percent; certificates were to be presented at a student reception on November 3.

**Prior minutes**
October 5, 2010 meeting: President Underwood presiding, Mr. Hauff absent, about 22 audience members. Motion 10-103 approved the consent agenda (6-0), including a leave request from Morse Elementary principal Judy Hunsberger; Motion 10-104 approved the 2010/2011 Sex Education Advisory Board membership (6-0); Motion 10-105 cancelled the November 2, 2010 meeting (6-0); Motion 10-106 moved to closed session for negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(h). More than 350 students were honored for AP exam performance; Anne Mull reported 35 states including Michigan had adopted the Common Core standards as of September 1, 2010; Mark Rajter reported the MPSERS lawsuit placing the 3% employee contribution in escrow and the Office of Retirement Services' 8% assumed rate of return. The October 12, 2010 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 8:55 p.m.

**Check register and other items**
The September register totals $3,732,969.93, with Fund 101 at $2,942,576.80 and the largest checks going to MESSA ($1,167,780.10) and MPSERS ($887,179.37). Bid Award #9694 for copy paper went to Midland Paper at $64,950.48. Jennifer Messacar was recommended for a probationary contract as .8 FTE language arts teacher at Larson Middle School. Jennifer Taylor and Troy High senior Lynsey Mukomel presented APT to Succeed. Teresa Pollock of Plante & Moran presented the 2009/2010 audit for acceptance, and the Board considered Troy Youth Assistance by-law changes revised October 14, 2010.
2010_012_101910regmtg.verbose:
**Identity and agenda.** Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting packet for Tuesday, October 19, 2010, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district masthead 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. The consent agenda (p. 9) carries October 5 meeting minutes, October 12 workshop minutes, the September 2010 Treasurer's Report and the copy paper bid award; later items are Personnel (p. 82), the APT to Succeed curriculum report (p. 84), the 2009/2010 Audit report and consideration (pp. 98-99) and Troy Youth Assistance By-Law Revisions (p. 100).

**Recognitions.** Martell Elementary fifth graders won last year's Red Ribbon Song Contest, sponsored by Troy Families for Safe Homes and The Troy Coalition; the song "Don't Let Drugs Get in the Way of Your Dreams" is credited to Martell fourth graders of Mrs. Childress, Mr. Francis and Mr. Maliepaard with teacher Andrea Moon, October, 2009. Bemis vocal music teacher Emily Jambeau announced a first-ever district-wide Fourth Grade Hit Song Contest. A resolution dated the nineteenth day of October, 2010 honors forty-two National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists: Ismail Ali, Rajeev Bhatt, Allison Chen, Christopher Chen, Laura Cheng, Joy Chiang, Jennifer Chuang, Susan Dong, Tanvi Gangal, Meherab Grewak, Sara Guenther, Ian Hartwig, Bojing Jia, James Jiang, Joyce Jih, Goutham Kapa, Nafeesa Khan, Nikita Kulkami, Ian Lai, Carmen Lee, Mason Liang, Nina Lu, Christina Manceor, Elizabeth Mutter, Mihir Pande, Shaina Sekhri, Yunus Shabandri, Jerald Shi, Raghav Subramaniam, Frank Tan, Saketh Tummala, Kaushik Varadarajan, Anita Vasudevan, Chharitha Veerapaneni, Gautham Vellaichamy, Shela Wang, Suola Wang, Brenda Wu, Jason Xie, George Yu, Wei Zhang and Xiao Zhu. More than one million students from some 22,000 high schools entered, 16,000 were named semifinalists, and status reflects scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT; copies were to be presented at a student reception on November 3.

**Minutes, October 5, 2010.** President Underwood called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo present and Mr. Hauff absent; Superintendent Fowler, administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Mull, Rajter, Stromayer and Witt, and about 22 audience members attended. More than 350 Troy students were honored by the College Board in four award categories; juniors Raymond Chen, Mason Liang and Xiao Zhu were recognized as National AP Scholars, which requires an average grade of four and eight or more AP exams. Motion 10-103 (Philippart/Edmunds) approved the September 21 minutes, September 28 workshop minutes and a leave request from Judy Hunsberger, principal of Morse Elementary, ayes 6, nays 0. Anne Mull, Director of Instruction & Assessment, presented the Common Core State Standards for K-12 ELA and mathematics, noting all states except Alaska and Texas supported initial development, 35 states including Michigan had adopted them as of September 1, 2010, and the ACT is the likely model for assessing grades 3-8 ahead of a 2014/2015 rollout. Motion 10-104 (Pochodylo/Fleming) approved the 2010/2011 Sex Education Advisory Board membership, 6-0. Mark Rajter's legislative update covered the MPSERS lawsuit over the 3% employee contribution held in escrow by injunction, the Ed Jobs Act awaiting the Governor's action, and the Office of Retirement Services' 8% assumed rate of return. Cindy Shankin of Boulan Park Middle School reported 110 backpacks provided by Troy teachers through the TEA program and delivered by Troy People Concerned. Motion 10-105 (Fleming/Miletti) cancelled the November 2, 2010 meeting, 6-0. Mrs. Fleming publicized the TFEE Annual Fun Walk of Saturday, October 23, 2010, walk at 10:00 a.m. at Troy High, 248-823-4035; Dr. Fowler cited Niles Class of 2001 graduate Pamela Heuer as one of 40 educators on NBC's Education Nation. Motion 10-106 entered closed session for negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(h), 6-0; closed session began 7:54 p.m., reconvened 8:44 p.m., adjourned 8:45 p.m. Submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary. The October 12, 2010 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 8:55 p.m. with Ms. Pollack, Ms. Edwards and Ms. Day of Plante & Moran and District Accountant Tolan present, covering the district audit, the Oakland County Regional Special Education Transportation Study and robo calls.

**Treasurer's Report, September 2010.** From Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, 4400 Livernois, 248-823-4022, dated October 5, 2010. **Remaining agenda items.** Bid Award #9694, copy paper: memo of October 14, 2010 from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077, to Mark S. Rajter; bids opened October 14, 2010, sent to 16 potential bidders with 16 responding, two of which were No Bid; recommended award to Midland Paper at $64,950.48 as a 2010/11 General Fund expenditure. Personnel: a probationary contract for 2010-2011 to Jennifer Messacar, .8 FTE language arts teacher at Larson Middle School, B.A. Oakland University December 2004, Michigan Professional Certificate September 2010, previously with Temporary Schools Staff and Oakland Christian Schools. Curriculum: Jennifer Taylor of Boulan Park Middle School and Troy High senior Lynsey Mukomel presented APT to Succeed, the academic achievement, personal management and teamwork portfolio program spanning grades 6-8 in which Troy Chamber of Commerce volunteers interview eighth graders each spring, introduced by Dr. Rich Machesky. Business: Teresa Pollock of Plante & Moran reported on the 2009-2010 audit, drafted for the October 12, 2010 workshop, with a resolution to accept the audited 2010 financial statements. Other: adoption of Troy Youth Assistance by-law changes to comply with Michigan requirements for a charitable raffle license, certified by Nancy L. Philippart. The attached by-laws, Articles I through XXIV, record sponsorship by the City of Troy, the Troy School District and the Oakland County Circuit Court-Family Division; creation by City of Troy Resolution #58-183, by the Troy School District on March 18, 1958 and by the Oakland County Probate Court on April 2, 1958, the court sponsor becoming the Circuit Court-Family Division on January 1, 1998; 501(c)(3) status; a Board of Directors limited to thirty members serving three-year terms, two consecutive; officers elected each May to two-year terms; amendments by two-thirds vote with ten days' written notice; eleven standing committees; and appended policies allowing line items up to $100.00 without Executive Committee approval (December 10, 2003), external financial reviews every three to five years (September 20, 2007), and a revision date of October 14, 2010.
